name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,788

clue.text: Steal animal's morsel

blocks.note: to snip is slang for to nick or pinch, i.e. steal
a pet is a domestic animal; the 's joins it on

explanation.surface: A thief makes off with some creature's dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's reads as ownership of the morsel, but it only glues PET onto SNIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both name a small piece or scrap of something, usually snipped off a larger whole.

clue.text: Mo Salah's top clips noted abroad

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter
letters sent abroad are scattered far and wide, out of their order

blocks.note: first letter of Salah
CLIPS NOTED rearranged

explanation.surface: Highlights of the Liverpool footballer Mohamed Salah, watched in foreign countries.
explanation.walkthrough: Mo reads as Mohamed Salah's nickname, but it is the short word for a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British 'mo' is short for moment, as in 'wait a mo'; both mean an instant of time.

clue.text: At home, one assumes Mum exercises well

indicators.note: to assume is to put on, like a garment, so SH goes on top of A

blocks.note: in = at home
mum = silent, as in 'keep mum'; SH asks for silence
a = one
PE = physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: A child notes that their mother, who works out, is fit and at home.
explanation.walkthrough: Mum looks like a mother; here it means silent, the sense in 'mum's the word'.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: someone fit and healthy is in good physical condition, i.e. well.

clue.text: Prunes and other fruit delivered

indicators.note: a speech is delivered, so the word is spoken rather than written

blocks.note: pears are fruit other than prunes

explanation.surface: Prunes and more fruit arrive by delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: Prunes looks like a fruit, which makes 'other fruit' natural, but it is the verb: to cut back.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a gardener who prunes trims or cuts back growth, just as a cook trims peel.

clue.text: Extremely anxious fool's suspect ethics

indicators.note: suspect means dubious, not to be trusted as it stands, so rearrange

blocks.note: a twit is a fool; the 's joins it on
ETHICS rearranged

explanation.surface: A fool with dodgy morals becomes deeply nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: Suspect reads as describing the fool's morals; it is telling you to rearrange ETHICS.
explanation.definitionFit: Twitchy is informal for nervous and jumpy; the superlative form matches 'extremely'.

clue.text: Perhaps Norma had some food - a common function

indicators.note: perhaps signals that Norma is one example of a wider class
held in common: the A is shared by both words and written once

blocks.note: Norma is Bellini's OPERA; its final A is the shared one
the A both words have in common
ATE = had some food, its A already supplied

explanation.surface: A woman called Norma took a bite, as everyone does.
explanation.walkthrough: OPERA and ATE overlap on one A, and 'a common' tells you to write it once.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as verbs: a machine that works or runs is functioning.

clue.text: Not yet settled or not quite married?

blocks.note: a bill still outstanding, not paid off
read as O plus WED: a nought before 'married', so nothing like wed

explanation.surface: A couple whose relationship is unresolved: are they married or not?
explanation.walkthrough: Settled suggests settling down with a partner, but it means paid. The question mark flags the whimsical O-WED reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt still outstanding remains unpaid; the second half is a playful split into a zero and a wedding.

clue.text: Once abstinent drifter admitted becoming party animal?

indicators.note: TT admits, or lets in, the drifter, so ROVER goes inside

blocks.note: ex = former, once
TT = teetotal, abstaining from drink
a rover wanders about

explanation.surface: A reformed drinker, once a wanderer, lets loose and becomes the life of the party.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks party animal as a loose, playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: an outgoing, sociable person is the sort who loves a party.

clue.text: Fits current trousers

blocks.note: AC = alternating current
cords = corduroy trousers

explanation.surface: A shopper finds that today's fashionable trousers fit.
explanation.walkthrough: Fits and current both pose as clothing words; current is electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as verbs: to agree or be consistent with, as a story matches the facts.

clue.text: Flip cover that's slippery

definitions.note: slippery is an adjective; with 'that's' it describes the thing, a noun

indicators.note: to flip something is to turn it over, so the word runs back up

blocks.note: lee = shelter, cover from the wind

explanation.surface: A lid that flips over turns out to be slick.
explanation.walkthrough: Flip cover suggests a phone case; cover is shelter, as in the lee of a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the fish's smooth, mucus-coated skin makes it proverbially hard to grasp.

clue.text: Nobody's free to swap spectacles for monocle 'by right'

indicators.note: to swap is to exchange: two lenses (OO) traded for one lens (O)
by means beside, so R is placed next to the rest

blocks.clueFragment: free to swap spectacles for monocle
blocks.note: LOOSE (free) with OO, two lenses, replaced by O, one lens
R = right

explanation.surface: A nobody may trade their glasses for an eyeglass, as is their right.
explanation.walkthrough: OO looks like a pair of spectacles and O like a monocle, so the swap turns LOOSE into LOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: an unsuccessful, insignificant person is dismissed as a nobody.

clue.text: Papers misrepresented a client's twin

indicators.note: the letters are presented wrongly, out of their proper order

blocks.note: ID = identity papers
A CLIENT rearranged

explanation.surface: Newspapers got a client's twin sibling wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Papers are identity documents, not newspapers; twin is an adjective here.
explanation.definitionFit: As adjectives both mean exactly matching, as twin beds or matching pairs are.

clue.text: Negotiate gender reassignment legislation?

blocks.note: trans = transgender
an act is a piece of legislation

explanation.surface: Politicians haggle over a law on changing gender.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that the answer is being split playfully into a law about gender.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as verbs: to conduct business or carry through a deal.

clue.text: Foul made by Rodri in action against Hearts

indicators.note: something in action is moving about, so Rodri's letters shift
against can mean up next to, so H is placed beside the result

blocks.note: H = hearts, the card suit
RODRI rearranged

explanation.surface: A match report: the midfielder Rodri commits a foul against the Scottish club Hearts.
explanation.walkthrough: Foul is the football offence in the surface but the adjective nasty in the answer. Hearts is an Edinburgh football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as adjectives: nasty, very unpleasant or disgusting.

clue.text: Conflict in shared bedroom occupied by bewildered setters

indicators.note: a room occupied by people has them inside it, so the dorm holds the letters
the setters are confused, their letters jumbled

blocks.note: a dorm (dormitory) is a shared bedroom
SETTERS rearranged

explanation.surface: Confused crossword setters squabble in the dormitory they share.
explanation.walkthrough: Operation Desert Storm was the 1991 Gulf War campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the 1991 Gulf War operation against Iraq was a military conflict.

clue.text: Teenage gamine periodically sought for modelling contract

indicators.note: at regular periods: take every other letter
modelling clay is shaping it, so the letters are shaped into a new form

blocks.note: taken as it stands
G_M_N_ from gamine

explanation.surface: A young, boyishly slim girl is scouted for a modelling deal.
explanation.walkthrough: Modelling belongs to the fashion picture, but it is the instruction to reshape the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer's booking or job is an agreed arrangement, a contract for work.

clue.text: Face-lift: what does it achieve?

blocks.note: one face of a building, as an architect draws it
raising, a lift
surface padding: a question whose joking answer is the entry itself

explanation.surface: A question about what cosmetic surgery actually accomplishes.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen welds two definitions into one cosmetic procedure, and the question adds a third reading: a face-lift achieves elevation.
explanation.definitionFit: An architect's drawing of one side of a building, and also the act of raising something higher.

clue.text: Sex during tap dancing used contorting abilities

indicators.note: during means in the course of, so IT falls within the two rearranged words
letters that dance move about, so TAP takes a new order
to contort is to twist out of shape, so USED is twisted

blocks.note: TAP rearranged
it = sex, as in 'doing it'
USED rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheeky picture of tap dancers showing off how flexible they are.
explanation.walkthrough: Tap dancing reads as the dance style, but dancing is an instruction applied to TAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: natural talents or skills, a knack for doing something.

clue.text: Drops off suits when leaving Poland

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so the letters for Poland depart the word

blocks.note: suits = pleases, as in 'that suits me'
PL is the international code for Poland; removed

explanation.surface: Someone nods off whenever it's convenient to depart from Poland.
explanation.walkthrough: Suits reads as clothing or court cases; it is the verb, pleases.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as verbs: lessens or slackens, as rain or demand gradually declines.

clue.text: Corporation's e-ticketing limits start

indicators.note: to limit is to bound, so the phrase holds the answer within its bounds

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of Corporation's into the start of e-ticketing

explanation.surface: A company's electronic ticketing puts caps on something.
explanation.walkthrough: Limits reads as restrictions on e-ticketing; it means contains.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the beginning of something, especially an illness or winter.

clue.text: Queen interrupting settles protests

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break in, so QU breaks into the middle of SEALS

blocks.note: seals = settles, as in 'seal the deal'
Qu. is an abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: The monarch steps in to calm down demonstrations.
explanation.walkthrough: Protests looks like a noun for demonstrations; it is the verb, complains.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as verbs: complains loudly, objects shrilly to something unfair.

clue.text: Darker Cornish paintings maybe more popular if very quietly forgotten

indicators.note: maybe signals that paintings are one example of a wider class
what is forgotten is left out, so PP drops from the word

blocks.note: Cornwall is in the South West (SW) of England
paintings are art

blocks.clueFragment: more popular if very quietly forgotten
blocks.note: HIPPIER (more popular, trendier) without PP, the musical mark for very quietly

explanation.surface: Cornish paintings might sell better if they were a bit darker and less muted.
explanation.walkthrough: PP (pianissimo) is the musical direction for very quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Swarthy describes a dark complexion or skin; the comparative form matches 'darker'.

clue.text: Frozen wildernesses found over in Room 101

indicators.note: turned over in a down entry, the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: room = space
CI = 101 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Icy wastes turn up inside Orwell's torture chamber, Room 101.
explanation.walkthrough: Room 101 is the torture room in Orwell's 1984, but the clue splits it into ROOM and 101.
explanation.definitionFit: Polar sheets of permanent ice cover huge uninhabited regions, frozen wastes.

clue.text: Suspects party underlings blame the SNP's leaders

indicators.note: leaders go at the front, so take the leading letter of each word

blocks.note: a do is a party
first letters of underlings, blame, the, SNP's

explanation.surface: Party juniors point the finger at the Scottish National Party's leadership.
explanation.walkthrough: Leaders looks like party bosses, but it picks the first letter of each word. The SNP is the Scottish National Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as verbs: mistrusts, is inclined to disbelieve something.

clue.text: Takes off underpants in interviews?

blocks.note: briefs are underpants, and the prefix de- means remove
questions someone after a mission

explanation.surface: Someone removes their underwear during questioning.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a pun: read the answer as DE-BRIEFS, and the question mark admits it.
explanation.definitionFit: Questioning an agent or soldier after a completed mission; the joke half reads it as removing briefs.

clue.text: Wild storm engulfs the centre of Newbury

indicators.note: to engulf is to swallow up, so RAID closes around the letter
the centre of a word is its middle letter

blocks.note: to storm a place is to raid it
middle letter of NEWBURY

explanation.surface: A fierce storm sweeps over the middle of the Berkshire town of Newbury.
explanation.walkthrough: Wild and storm pose as weather; storm is the verb, to attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: frenzied and uncontrolled, like a dog with rabies.

clue.text: Expressions of excitement issue over the Tannoy

indicators.note: a Tannoy is a public address system, so the word is spoken

blocks.note: to ooze is to issue, seep out

explanation.surface: An announcement over a loudspeaker sets off gasps of delight.
explanation.walkthrough: Issue looks like a noun, a problem; it is the verb, to flow out.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the delighted gasps a crowd lets out at fireworks.

clue.text: Showy elderly relative does initially impressive cartwheels

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is taken
the letters turn head over heels

blocks.note: gran = grandmother
DOES plus I, the first letter of impressive, rearranged

explanation.surface: A flamboyant grandmother pulls off some remarkable cartwheels.
explanation.walkthrough: The gran doing cartwheels is the joke; cartwheels is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: pretentiously grand, designed to impress, ostentatious.

clue.text: Fishy item in bagging area

indicators.note: in means inside, so the answer sits within the phrase

blocks.note: the last letter of bagging and the first two of area

explanation.surface: The self-checkout machine complains of an unexpected item in the bagging area.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes the self-checkout warning 'unexpected item in bagging area'.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a long-snouted freshwater fish, so a fishy item.

clue.text: Vote against party

blocks.note: voting against means casting a negative ballot, read as a three-word phrase
a celebration, not a political party

explanation.surface: Voting against a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as BE A NO for the first half. Party reads as political, but a beano is British slang for a knees-up.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a noisy celebration or knees-up; split into three words it is what a dissenting voter does.

clue.text: Checks Nadal's OK to be introduced to supporters

indicators.note: introduced to means put into, so SI goes inside RESTS

blocks.note: rests = supports, as for a snooker cue
si is Spanish for yes; Rafael Nadal is Spanish

explanation.surface: Rafael Nadal is happy to be introduced to his fans.
explanation.walkthrough: Nadal is the Spanish tennis player, so his OK is the Spanish si.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as verbs: holds back or withstands, as a dam stems a flood.

clue.text: Healthy reward a few gathered after clean-up

indicators.note: what you gather is what you hear, as in 'I gather'
after means following, so this part comes second

blocks.note: a tidy is a clean-up
some = a few

explanation.surface: A handful of volunteers collect a generous payment after a litter pick.
explanation.walkthrough: Gathered looks like collecting people; it means heard, as in 'I gather'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a large amount of money, so a generous payment or prize.
